subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep Host-header origin fallback as a dangerous operator-selected mode, remove it, or keep it only with an additional CSRF/DNS-rebinding defense?
rationale: The remaining behavior is an intentional documented escape hatch in a Gateway security boundary; changing it affects compatibility and operator policy, while accepting it leaves a known downgrade in exposed deployments.

options.title: Harden break-glass mode
options.body: Keep the existing flag but add targeted defenses and tests for DNS-rebinding/Host-header fallback without breaking documented loopback flows.

options.title: Remove the flag
options.body: Delete the fallback and add doctor/docs/test coverage for users who previously relied on it.

options.title: Accept audit-only posture
options.body: Leave runtime behavior as-is and treat critical audit findings plus docs as the supported operator warning model.

recommendation.title: Harden break-glass mode
recommendation.body: Keep the existing flag but add targeted defenses and tests for DNS-rebinding/Host-header fallback without breaking documented loopback flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Remote history shows the broadest recent work on gateway origin restrictions and security-hardening policy around this surface.
